headline: Approved a new tenant at 383 Middle Street; sent a negative zoning referral on earth excavation facilities; continued 107 Chestnut Street subdivision.
summary: A public hearing was set for November 23 on a manufacturing building at 681 Clark Avenue. A positive referral went to City Council on the city's sale of 190 Business Park Drive. The city also hired IMEG to update its Plan of Conservation and Development.

plain_text:
Bristol Planning Commission Regular Meeting of October 26, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 1 – 
 
BRISTOL PLANNING COMMISSION 
MINUTES 
REGULAR MEETING OF MONDAY OCTOBER 26, 2026 
By: Chairman Veits Time: 6:00 P.M. Place: City Hall 
   Council Chambers 
   111 North Main Street 
   First Floor 
 
ROLL CALL: 
 
MEMBERS NAME PRESENT ABSENT 
    
REGULAR MEMBERS: Chairman William Veits (Chairman) X  
 Vacant (Vice Chairman)   
 Jon Pose X  
 Tracey Bacchus X  
 Christopher Nardi, Secretary X  
 Kiana Small X  
    
ALTERNATE MEMBERS: Greg Klimek X  
 DeWayne Wynn X  
 Keith Odume X  
    
STAFF: Robert M. Flanagan, AICP, City Planner X  
 
1. Call to Order 
 
Per the order of Chairman Veits the meeting was called to order at 6:00 P.M. 
 
Chairman Veits reminded the Commission the next Regular Meeting of the Planning Commission  
is Monday, November 23, 2026. 
 
2. Pledge of Allegiance 
 
3. Public Participation 
 
4. Approval of Minutes 
 
a. Regular Meeting — September 28, 2026 
 
Chairman Veits designated regular Commissioners Pose, Bacchus, Nardi and Veits with alternate Commissioners Klimek to vote on 
the September 28, 2026, regular meeting minutes. 
 
MOTION: Move to approve the minutes of the September 28, 2026, regular meeting. 
 
By: Pose Seconded: Klimek. 
 
For: Klimek, Pose, Bacchus, Nardi and Veits. 
Against: None. 
Abstain: None.
Bristol Planning Commission Regular Meeting of October 26, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 2 – 
 
Chairman Veits designated regular Commissioners Nardi, Pose, Bacchus, Small and Veits as voting Commissioners this evening. 
 
5. Receipt of New Applications 
 
a. Application 456 — Site Plan application for the development of a manufacturing building consisting of 68,400 sq. ft. at 
681 Clark Avenue, Assessor's Map 66, Lot 261A-1+261A-2; Borghesi Building and Engineering, applicant; Stephen O. 
Allaire - Esquire, owner. 
 
Chairman Veits designated regular Commissioners Nardi, Pose, Bacchus, Small and Veits to vote on Application #456. 
 
Mr. Flanagan spoke with the applicant this morning and the applicant was aware a public hearing would be scheduled this evening. 
 
MOTION: Move that Application #456 be scheduled for a Public Hearing on Monday, November 23, 2026. 
 
By: Pose Seconded: Nardi. 
 
For: Nardi, Bacchus, Pose, Small and Veits. 
Against: None. 
Abstain: None. 
 
The application is scheduled for public hearing. 
 
6. Public Hearings 
a. Application #453 — Subdivision — 107 Chestnut Street (3 lots) Assessor’s Map 29, Lot 253/30; RM-5 (Mixed Residential) 
zone; Chestnut and Locust Holdings, LLC, owner/applicant — PUBLIC HEARING CONTINUED FROM SEPTEMBER 28, 2026. 
 
Chairman Veits designated regular Commissioners Nardi, Pose, Bacchus, Small and Veits to vote on Application #453. 
 
Charles Talmadge, consultant, of Development Planning Solutions, 225 North Main St., representing the applicant, explained at the 
September meeting the concern was the Commission wanted to review a development plan that was provided to Staff. Mr. 
Talmadge reviewed the recent comments the applicant was able to address.  
 
Mr. Talmadge indicated the stormwater easement on the west side of the property was revised. Mr. Talmadge noted the 230 ft. of 
water main line to bring to the site that was requested from the Water Dept. the applicant would like to review with their staff. 
The consultant noted the applicant would work with Staff to resolve the comments. 
 
The City Planner indicated the response comments were received this morning.  Mr. Flanagan said he wanted the Site Plan 
Committee to review the comments but they had not been distributed yet. The City Planner noted the applicant has time to extend 
the application to keep the Public Hearing open. 
 
Commission inquires: Mr. Talmadge said the applicant had to wait for their engineer to revise the plans. The consultant reviewed 
the two Fire Dept. comments. Mr. Talmadge noted one of the units would be at 46 Locust St. and one unit would be on the corner 
of Chestnut St. and Locust St. 
 
The consultant agreed on behalf of the applicant to extend the application 30-days to the November 2026 meeting. 
 
MOTION: Move to accept the 30-day extension of the Public Hearing for Application #453 to the next Regular Meeting of the 
Planning Commission on November 23, 2026. 
 
Note: The applicant will need to assign 30-days to extend the application to get to the November 23, 2026 meeting.
Bristol Planning Commission Regular Meeting of October 26, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 3 – 
 
By: Bacchus Seconded: Pose. 
 
For: Nardi, Bacchus, Pose, Small and Veits. 
Against: None. 
Abstain: None. 
 
The application is continued. 
 
7. Zoning Commission Referrals 
 
a. Application #2577 — Proposed amendments to the Zoning Regulations to add an Earth Excavation and Reclamation 
Facility use: 1. Delete Article III, Section 15.2.4.A.1. I-General Industrial zone; 2. Add Section 15.7 Permit Duration – 
Industrial Zones Exceeding Twenty (20) acres with the following requirements: a. parcel must be a minimum of twenty 
(20) acres; b. subject to Special Permit and Site Plan applications; c. proposes that Special Permits to be valid for a period 
of nine (9) years; d. proposes the use be located in the (I) General Industrial zone. Attorney James Ziogas, applicant. 
 
Chairman Veits designated regular Commissioners Nardi, Pose, Bacchus, Small and Veits to vote on Application #2577. 
 
Attorney James Ziogas, 104 Bellevue Avenue stated that he started drafting the Regulation in February 2026 and there were a lot 
of changes and discussions with Staff and clients. Attorney Ziogas noted the request was to create an earth excavation and 
reclamation facility to be similar to the facility located in Farmington that sells reclaimed materials. The attorney mentioned there 
are none of these facilities in Bristol.  
 
Attorney Ziogas said the request was to create an amendment for a facility with 20 or more acres in an industrial zone. The 
attorney indicated with the equipment and infrastructure required by the time the business is started a 9-year approval was 
needed. The attorney mentioned usually there is an end use required but this was the end use of the property. Attorney Ziogas’ 
view was a facility was necessary in Bristol that is currently not allowed. 
 
Mr. Flanagan was not supportive of this amendment to the Regulations. The City Planner would hold any substantive comments he 
has for the public hearing during the Zoning Commission meeting.  
 
Commission inquiries: Attorney Ziogas highlighted the 20-acre sites would only be on a site to aggregate in an I-Zone neighbor-
hood. The attorney indicated if approved there would be a 9-year review for the Special Permit. Attorney Ziogas stated the 
applicant was close to acquiring a 20-acre site in the I-Zone that would require a Special Permit and Site Plan with the Zoning 
Commission. The attorney said the applicant would work around the inland wetland areas. Attorney Ziogas noted the request 
would Add Section 15.7 Permit Duration – Industrial Zones Exceeding Twenty (20) acres with the discussed requirements. 
 
MOTION: Move to send a negative referral to the Zoning Commission for: Application #2577 — Proposed amendments to the 
Zoning Regulations to add an Earth Excavation and Reclamation Facility use because the Planning Commission finds that 
the proposed text Amendment, as presented, is generally not consistent with the goals and policies of the 2015 Plan of 
Conservation and Development, amended to April 1, 2018. 
 
By: Bacchus Seconded: Small. 
 
Roll Call Vote: 
 
For: Nardi, Bacchus, Small and Veits. 
Against: Pose. 
Abstain: None.
Bristol Planning Commission Regular Meeting of October 26, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 4 – 
 
The CT General Statute 8-24 Referral was sent a negative referral. 
 
8. City Council and Other Referrals 
 
a. C.G.S. 8-24 Referral:  
190 Business Park Drive — Map 3, Lot 6 
 
Chairman Veits designated regular Commissioners Nardi, Pose, Bacchus, Small and Veits to vote on C.G.S. 8-24 Referral: 190 
Business Park Drive — Map 3, Lot 6. 
 
Mr. Flanagan reviewed there was a C.G.S. 8-24 Referral for 190 Business Park Dr., that received an approval for a Site Plan from 
the Commission last month. The City Planner explained the request this evening was received from the City Council to sell the 
property. Mr. Flanagan requested Mr. Charles Talmadge to speak on behalf of the developer. 
 
Charles Talmadge of Development Planning Solutions, 225 North Main St., reviewed with Attorney James Ziogas an application for 
Site Plan for Integrity Manufacturing for a 29,000 sq. ft. facility at Business Park Dr. Mr. Talmadge said the request was for 
approval for the sale of the property by the City, but the developer had to have Site Plan approval before the sale of the property 
is final.  
 
MOTION: Move to send a positive referral to the City Council for the C.G.S. 8-24 referral for: 
190 Business Park Drive — Map 3, Lot 6. 
 
The Planning Commission finds that the C.G.S. 8-24 referral for the City of Bristol to sell the property at 190 Business Park Drive, 
Map 3, Lot 6 is generally consistent with the goals and policies of the 2015 Plan of Conservation and Development (POCD), 
amended to April 1, 2018. 
 
By: Small Seconded: Bacchus. 
 
For: Nardi, Bacchus, Pose, Small and Veits. 
Against: None. 
Abstain: None. 
 
The CT General Statute 8-24 Referral was sent a positive referral. 
 
9. New Business 
 
a. Application #442 — Revision to an Approved Site Plan for a Wholesale or Distribution Facility (new tenant — Unit 4A) 
consisting of 33,000 sq. ft. at 383 Middle Street; Assessor's Map 3, Lot 35; IP-1 (Industrial Park) zone; Bloom Bristol, LLC, 
applicant/owner. 
 
Chairman Veits designated regular Commissioners Nardi, Pose, Bacchus, Small and Veits to vote on Application #442. 
 
Brian Baker, P.E. of Civil 1, 43 Sherman Hill Rd., Woodbury, representing the applicant, reminded the Commission the applicant 
had 2 applications previously for ESPN North Campus at 383 Middle St. and for unit #2 to the rear of the property. The engineer 
indicated a new tenant of fire and life safety and fire suppression company. Mr. Baker said the company would have wholesale and 
distribution facility to receive materials and parts. The engineer noted the facility would be repackaging items and equipment and 
sending the packages out from the facility.  
 
Mr. Baker said there would be more office than manufacturing area. The engineer added there was a required 957 parking spaces 
but 976 parking spaces was being provided. Mr. Baker noted there would be one door for the loading dock on unit 4 that was
Bristol Planning Commission Regular Meeting of October 26, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 5 – 
 
similar to unit 2. The engineer noted this tenant would be an allowed use for warehousing and distribution so the owner can go 
forward with this tenant. 
 
The City Planner was pleased the owner brought in some additional tenants for the building. Mr. Flanagan wanted the Commission 
to be aware of some of the applications with revisions in the Land Use Office.  
 
City Planner inquiries: Mr. Baker described the ESPN facility in the center of the property that was mostly media storage. The 
engineer noted there are only a few employees at the ESPN facility.  
 
MOTION: Move to approve Application #442 — Revision to an Approved Site Plan for a Wholesale or Distribution Facility (new 
tenant — Unit 4A) consisting of 33,000 sq. ft. at 383 Middle Street; Assessor's Map 3, Lot 35; IP-1 (Industrial Park) 
zone, with the following stipulations: 
 
1. The proposed Tenant use for Unit 4 primary use will be distribution and logistics with associated office functions and is 
consistent with the already approved use from June 2026. 
 
2. The proposed Tenant parking for Unit 4 does not require any changes to the site plan and the parking provided on-site 
remains sufficient. 
 
3. All site improvements which have not been satisfactorily completed by the time a Certificate of Occupancy is applied for shall 
be bonded in accordance with Article 4 Section 16.3.16. of the Zoning Regulations. The performance bond shall be posted by 
the applicant with the City before the Certificate of Completion being issued. 
 
By: Nardi Seconded: Bacchus. 
 
For: Nardi, Bacchus, Pose, Small and Veits. 
Against: None. 
Abstain: None. 
 
The application is approved. 
 
10. Old Business 
 
There was no old business. 
 
11. Staff Reports 
a. 2028 Bristol Plan of Conservation and Development 
 
The City Planner reviewed the members of the 2028 Bristol Plan of Conservation and Development Selection Committee. Mr. 
Flanagan said the Committee met with 5 consultants that applied for the project and the decision was to hire IMEG. The City 
Planner noted the consultant would update the POCD and the process will be 1 year from December 2026 to December 2027. 
Mr. Flanagan stated the meetings would be in person but the online Zoom component would be available for Commissioners who 
may be away on business and want to participate and for some special meetings. The City Planner would have a schedule for the 
Commission at the November meeting.  
 
b. Subdivision Status Report — October 2026 
 
The City Planner highlighted there were no changes to the Subdivision Status Report.  
 
12. Communications
Bristol Planning Commission Regular Meeting of October 26, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 6 – 
 
 
Mr. Flanagan added that Commissioner Small was appointed as a regular Commissioner and Commissioner Odume was appointed 
as an alternate Commissioner. The Commission welcomed Commissioner Odume to the Commission. 
 
Chairman Veits congratulated the Commissioners on their appointments. 
 
13. Adjournment 
 
Motion was made by Commissioner Pose to adjourn. 
Motion seconded by Commissioner Bacchus. 
Motion carried 5-0. 
 
The meeting adjourned at 6:45 P.M. 
 
 
These minutes represent the proceedings of the meeting. 
This meeting was recorded. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
Nancy King 
 
 
 
 
William Veits 
Chairman 
City Planning Commission
